---
title: "The booklet: it sells and it promises"
unit: 5
module: 3
duration: "10 min"
---

<Phase type="activation">

Picture a restaurant menu where the dishes have no prices and no ingredients. Only beautiful photos and the words "tender" and "unforgettable".

**Would you order — or ask the waiter what is really in it?** Think about what you would ask first.

</Phase>

<Phase type="reflection">

Go back to the menu without prices or ingredients. People want to know what they get and what it costs. Beauty helps them choose, but it does not answer the questions.

**A retreat booklet does two jobs at once: it sells the week and it promises what is in it.** Guests later read the second part more closely than the first.

</Phase>

<Phase type="concept">

## One page, two jobs

The booklet invites: it tells about the place, the people, the change. It also fixes the terms: what the price includes, what it does not, how to pay, when a refund is possible. If the booklet says nothing, the guest fills the gap on their own. That is exactly where disputes start.

## Pick your guest right away

The first page answers the question "is this for me?". Who the week is for and who it will not suit — from unit u1. A person who recognises themselves reads on. Someone it does not suit leaves at once, and that is good for both.

## What you will go through, and why

A list of "yoga, meditation, walks" describes a timetable, not a week. Next to each item, write what it serves: which part of the guest's change it supports. This is how it gets from module 04 into the booklet.

## Included and not included is a promise

Booklets that sell well write both lists. Usually not included: the trip to the place, food on arrival day, personal spending, insurance. What is not in "included", the guest does not expect. What is there, they have a right to ask for.

## How to book: the form before the money

A good order: application, a short call, the guest form, the deposit, a confirmed place. The form before payment shows contraindications and diets before any money changes hands. If the guest is not a fit, the deposit is refunded in full.

## Honest words

No promises of healing or results — as with the practice card. Testimonials only with the author's consent. Photos of the venue only with the venue's permission. Urgency like "two places left" only if it is true.

## A booklet from your own numbers

Dates, price, deposit, payment and cancellation dates are already in the calculator and the timeline. The [retreat booklet](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/buklet/#) pulls them in by link and warns you if something has drifted or is missing. What is left is to write the texts, add photos and save a PDF.

## The same page online

A booklet is sent to a person; a sign-up page is where newsletters and social posts lead. It is the same data in another form: the [retreat landing page](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/lending/) is built from the booklet draft, with a sign-up button, a subtitle and a couple of key numbers added.

The sign-up button leads to the guest form or a messenger — not to payment. Cancellation terms and "not included" are required on the page just as in the booklet. Real retreat pages most often lack them, and that is exactly where disputes start later.

<SelfCheck id="c5"/>

</Phase>

<Phase type="practice">

1. Open the [practice booklet](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/buklet/#) and read the list of errors above the preview.
2. Find which section is missing for the booklet to become a contract. Add it.
3. Write "who it is for" and "who it will not suit" for your retreat — three lines each.
4. Move three practices from your programme into "what you will go through" and add what each one serves.
5. Make the "included" and "not included" lists. Check that nothing is left that a guest could read two ways.
6. Open the retreat landing page, put your guest form address into the sign-up button and download the page. Open the file on your phone.

</Phase>
